filename: Crowdsourcing the Frontier_ Advancing Hybrid Physics-ML Climate Simulation via a $50,000 Kaggle Competition.pdf
title: Crowdsourcing the Frontier: Advancing Hybrid Physics‐ML Climate Simulation via a $50,000 Kaggle Competition
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
parameterization_target: Subgrid convective, microphysical, turbulent, and radiative tendencies (temperature, water vapor, cloud condensate, and wind tendencies, plus surface radiative and precipitation fluxes)
code_availability: The GitHub repository associated with this work is available via Apache License 2.0 and developed openly at https://github.com/leap-stc/climsim-kaggle-edition. The version of E3SM-MMF made compatible with FTorch is available at https://github.com/leap-stc/E3SM_nvlab. All models, checkpoints, and normalization files are uploaded to Hugging Face and are available at https://hf.co/collections/jlin404/climsim-kaggle-models. Software repositories, online simulation output, and various online simulation metadata are preserved at https://zenodo.org/records/18883121.
testbed_rationale: Evaluates 90 ML parameterization models across 6 diverse neural architectures and 5 configurations both offline and dynamically coupled online inside E3SM-MMF, with full microphysics coupling, open code, open weights on Hugging Face, and simulation data on Zenodo.
pain_points: Online instability and numerical crashes for certain architecture-configuration combinations (e.g., transformer-encoder models under expanded input lists)
Disconnect between offline R2 improvements and prognostic online performance/stability
Stubborn, shared systematic biases across all architectures (underprediction of tropical precipitable water and extreme precipitation; warm polar upper-level bias)
Significant inter-seed variability in online stability and drift requiring multi-seed ensembles
GPU memory management issues (FTorch out-of-memory errors due to omitted torch_delete)
High computational cost of full-scale online hybrid simulations and CRM data generation
extraction_notes: The paper assesses architectures adapted from the 2024 LEAP ClimSim Kaggle competition (Squeezeformer, Pure ResLSTM, Pao Model, ConvNeXt, Encoder-Decoder LSTM) against the U-Net baseline from Hu et al. (2025) across 5 configurations and 3 random seeds (90 models total).
